Epistemic Grounding: The Dualistic Nature of Types, Class Representability, and Expressions
Notation is fragile—always consult program/types/typetheory.ML for semantics rather than surface syntax. In Obelisk, we rigorously disambiguate four foundational principles:
  • 1. The Dualistic (at least!) Nature of Types (Syntactic AST vs. Semantic Predicate on Classes): Every type in typetheory.ML has at least a dualistic nature: (a) Syntactically, a type is an expression syntax tree (Small.Col.Expression or Huge.Col.Expression, constructed via OpSet, OpClass, OpFamily, OpConstructor); (b) Semantically, a type corresponds to a predicate on classes (LPredicate / Class -> Bool, via LTpEmb / Emb). Thus \( \mathrm{CLASS}(\mathrm{V}) \) is a well-formed mathematical formula inside the object theory, and in fact a theorem (\( \vdash \mathrm{CLASS}(\mathrm{V}) \), asserting that the universal class V satisfies the class predicate), which is distinct from the metalevel typing judgment (V : Class) or \( (\mathcal{W} : \mathsf{Theory}) \). Similarly, \( \mathrm{SET}(\emptyset) \) is a theorem, while \( \neg\mathrm{SET}(\mathrm{V}) \) is Russell's theorem.
  • 2. Types Representable by a Class vs. Proper Conglomerate Types (“When You Can Write Both : and ∈”):
    • Representable by a Class: Sometimes a type's semantic predicate holds only on sets belonging to a single class—for instance, Set is represented by the universal class V = {x | isSet(x)}, and syntactic datatypes of finite syntax trees (such as Class.Expression, Fm, Stmt, Prf) are representable by code classes in V_ω ⊂ V via Gödel encoding Enc. Because Class.Expression is a datatype of finite syntax trees (and representable by a class), for a class term expression t (such as \( (t = \langle x \rangle) \), the AST node embedding variable x) you can write both the typing judgment \( (t : \mathsf{Class.Expression}) \) and the membership formula \( (t \in \mathsf{Class.Expression}) \).
    • Not Representable by a Class (Proper Conglomerates): Other times, a type's predicate holds on proper classes (such as Class itself, where CLASS(X) ↔ ⊤). Its extension is a proper conglomerate (Huge.Col) that is not representable by any class in Morse–Kelley or NBG (since there is no class of all classes)—and that is completely fine! For a class variable x, you write the typing judgment \( (x : \mathsf{Class}) \) (or predicate CLASS(x)), but you cannot write x ∈ Class.
  • 3. The “Off-by-One” (Shift-to-Term, n → n+1) Level Rule & SML Kernel Type Glossary: Standard ML cannot store arbitrary mathematical classes or sets in memory; therefore level-0 mathematical sorts are uninhabited phantom types at SML runtime (type Class = Nonstored.t, type Set = Nonstored.t, where Nonstored.t = Void.t has no runtime values), and SML shifts every level n to level n+1 by storing syntactic expressions of those objects:
    • A.t = Nonstored.t: The abstract level-0 mathematical sort (e.g. Class.t, Truth.t, Theory.t), uninhabited at SML runtime.
    • A_Expre (Class_Expre, Fm_Expre = Truth_Expre, Theory_Expre): The SML head-constructor datatype (HC, HP, HA, HI) for compound expressions of sort A.
    • A.Expression.t = A_Expre sion: The full recursive SML AST wrapping A_Expre with metavariables (EVar), quotation (EInject), antiquotation (EAnti), evaluation (EEval), substitution (ESubst), and conditionals (EIf).
    • Fm = Truth.Expression.t and Ctx = XCtx of Fm list: Formula syntax trees and finite hypothesis contexts. Decidable side conditions on these ASTs are directly executable boolean functions in CakeML and Poly/ML.
  • 4. Turnstiles, Undecidable Provability vs. Decidable Proof Checking, & Theorems:
    • Exact Order of the Turnstile Relation: A sequent statement is written T, Γ ⊢ φ (or equivalently Γ ⊢_T φ): it is a ternary relation between Theory T (\(\mathcal{T} : \mathsf{Theory}\)), Context Γ (\(\Gamma : \mathsf{Ctx}\)), and Formula φ (\(\phi : \mathsf{Fm}\)), represented in the SML kernel by Stmt_p = ApStmt of Theory * Ctx * Fm.
    • Why Provability is Undecidable while Proof Checking is Decidable: Existential provability (∃(p : Prf), p : ProofOf(T, Γ ⊢ φ), i.e. whether there exists a proof of φ from T, Γ) is undecidable in general: for consistent finitely axiomatized theories extending Robinson arithmetic (including τ_NBG and τ_MK) it is Σ^0_1-complete by Church–Turing–Gödel; for higher-order subsystem F it is Δ^1_1-hard; and for an arbitrary semantic theory parameter W : Theory (which may be uncountable or non-r.e.) it is not even recursively enumerable. By contrast, proof verification (checking whether a given proof term p : Prf witnesses statement s : Stmt, i.e. Enc(p) ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(s))) is primitive recursive and decidable.
    • Material Implication Connective vs. Function Class (Dual Meaning of →) vs. Sequent Turnstile (⊢):
      • Syntactic Meaning of → (Variant 1 / Propositional Connective): Inside object-language formulas (Fm), → (constructor TpImpl : Fm * Fm -> Fm) is the binary propositional connective forming an implication formula ((φ → ψ) : Fm).
      • Semantic Meaning of → (Variant 2 / Class of Functions & Curry–Howard): On classes/sets (and in Variant 2 / type annotations), (A → B) denotes the class of functions from A to B: (A → B) := { f | (isClassFunction(f) ∧ ((Dom(f) = A) ∧ ∀x ((x ∈ A) → (f(x) ∈ B)))) } (which under Curry–Howard propositions-as-types also represents the space of proof transformations from A to B).
      • Sequent Turnstile (⊢): Constructor ApStmt : Theory * Ctx * Fm -> Stmt forming a sequent statement (T, Γ ⊢ φ). Turnstiles (⊢) must never be used where implication (→) is intended.
    • Statement vs. Theorem (Syntactical Variant 1, SML Kernel, & Semantical Variant 2): A Statement (s : Stmt) is a syntactic sequent T, Γ ⊢ φ. In the Syntactical Variant (Variant 1, 1st-Order), a Theorem is a dependent pair in the Sigma-type Σ(s : Stmt) ProofOf(s) (with ProofOf(s) / ProofsOf(Enc(s)) typing the proof witness), which is implemented in Standard ML as the algebraic datatype datatype Thm = Thm of Stmt.Expression * Prf. In the Semantical Variant (Variant 2, Rocq-style Higher-Order), a formula φ is a type directly, so a theorem is simply Theorem name : φ := prf without needing ProofOf.
    • Why ∀(T : Type) is Replaced by Metalevel Syntactic Quantification ∀(T_e : Type_Expression), … &llbracket;T_e&rrbracket; …: In semantic MK/NBG class theory, quantifying over all semantic types (∀(T : Type)) is strictly forbidden because type Type = Nonstored.t has no semantic carrier class (avoiding Girard’s / Russell’s paradox). Therefore, type-polymorphic rules (such as 3.23 simple_if, 3.24 if_dep, 4.01, and 4.02) quantify on the metalevel over syntactic type expressions ∀(T_e : Type_Expression) and use valuation brackets &llbracket;T_e&rrbracket; (or ASCII [|T_e|] from program/libs/unicodedefs.ML) to evaluate the syntactic type expression T_e into a semantic type inside the formula. Similarly, for theories (6.01), Model(W) (CpEnc in typetheory.ML) maps a syntactic theory expression (W : Theory) to its corresponding class term so (Model(W) ⊆ Model(Q)) is well-typed. Use the Type Quantification switch below to toggle between these notations.
Mathematical Architecture: Semantic Formulas, Side Conditions (NFV & FFI), and Catalog Conventions

In the Obelisk Proof Assistant, mathematical set/class semantics and syntactic metalevel side conditions are formally and rigorously decoupled:

  • The Two Real Interpretations (Set/Class Model vs. Executable SML Code): We strictly distinguish between (1) Meaning in Model inside MK/NBG (pure mathematical assertions: \( \forall X \), \( \forall (x \in \mathrm{V}) \), \( \mathrm{isSet}(x) \), avoiding any pseudo-membership like ∈ Theory or ∈ Class), and (2) Checkable / Executable Code in CakeML and Poly/ML (Standard ML AST expressions: Class_Expre, Fm_Expre, Theory_Expre, Ctx). Use the Interpretation switch in the header to view either representation.
  • Metatheoretic Variables \( (v_x, v_y, v_C, v_s) \) vs. Metatheoretic Constants \( (c_x, c_y, c_C) \) vs. Italic Red Class Variables & Upright Theory Symbols: When an arbitrary object-language variable is reasoned about schematically in a rule or side condition (such as \( (\mathrm{NFV}(v_C, \phi) = \mathrm{True}) \) or \( (\mathrm{FFI}(t, v_x, \phi) = \mathrm{True}) \)), it is represented by a metatheoretic variable \( (v_x : \mathsf{Variable}) \) in \( (v_x, v_y, v_C, v_s) \) (universally quantified on the metalevel over variable identifiers). By contrast, a fixed concrete variable identifier (such as Variable_id("x")) is denoted by a metatheoretic constant in \( (c_x, c_y, c_C) \). Constants (V for the universal class of all sets, On, ∅), functional symbols (ifdep, simple_if, sss, π1, π2), predicate symbols (isSet, isClassFunction, isUniverse, NFV, FFI), and theory symbols in general are rendered upright (not italicized), whereas class variables (\( X, Y, C, x, y, z \)) are rendered italicized in red (#f87171). When a formula makes sense specifically when a class variable denotes a set (for example on the left of ∈ or guarded by isSet(x)), we use lowercase (\( x, y, z, a, b, u, v \)) as a clean human-readable naming convention (never used by algorithms to decide semantics or typing).
  • Definitions of Decidable Side-Condition Predicates (NFV, FFI, Fresh):
    • NFV(v_x, φ) = True (“Not a Free Variable”): Variable identifier v_x does not occur free in formula AST φ (i.e. v_x ∉ FV(φ)), implemented by structural recursion in program/types/typetheory.ML and reflected in metatheory.html#nfv-prop.
    • FFI(t, v_x, φ) = True (“Free For Instantiation / Free For Substitution”): Term expression t is free for v_x in formula φ—no free variable of t becomes captured by any quantifier (∀, ∃) or class comprehension binder ({ z | ... }) when substituting t for free occurrences of v_x in φ (reflected in metatheory.html#ffi-quant).
    • Fresh(v_y, v_x) = True: Variable identifiers v_y and v_x are syntactically distinct (v_y ≠ v_x).
  • Formula Taxonomy (2×2 Terminology Switch), MK vs. NBG Switch, & Canonical entries.ML Numbering:
    • Terminology Switch (Row 1 below): Toggles between two standard naming conventions for closed vs. parameterized formulas: Mode A (Default) calls closed formulas without metavariables Formula and parameterized templates Formula Scheme; Mode B calls closed formulas Unschematic Formula and parameterized templates Formula.
    • Object Theory Switch (Row 2 below — MK vs. NBG): The kernel parameterizes class comprehension (3.01) by a boolean flag check_flag in program/types/foundations.ML (if check_flag then ... check_comprehension ... else ...): setting check_flag = false selects Morse–Kelley (τ_MK) (unrestricted impredicative comprehension over arbitrary formulas), while check_flag = true enforces von Neumann–Bernays–Gödel (τ_NBG) (predicative comprehension restricted to set-quantified formulas via check_comprehension).
    • Canonical Catalog Item Numbering & Explicit SML Kernel ID Mapping: Catalog item numbers (1.01–1.07, 2.01–2.05, 3.01–3.71, 4.01–4.13, 5.01–5.05, 6.01) are mapped via an explicit CATALOG_TO_SML_KERNEL_ID dictionary to their exact foundations.ML IDs in sml_kernel_export.json (e.g. catalog 3.35 → SML 3.40 lesseq_def_entry, catalog 3.36 → SML 3.41 card_def_entry, catalog 3.37 → SML 3.26 img_def_entry, catalog 3.38 → SML 3.42 less_def_entry, catalog 3.39 → SML 3.43 size_limitation_axm_entry, catalog 3.67–3.71 → SML 3.35–3.39).
📐 Surface Compiler Reference: formula <Name> = <Formula>; (Type) vs. theorem <Name> : <Formula> = <ProofTerm>; (Proof Term)

In Variant 2’s Curry–Howard surface language (examples/true_and_false_mk_guide.nbg, compiled by NBGSurfaceCompiler.compileSurfaceFile), formulas of Morse–Kelley / NBG are Types (NBGCompiler.Type) and proofs are explicit Kernel Terms (NBGCompiler.Expr):

1. Defining a Formula (Type) — True & False Alike
(* Defining a formula ONLY defines a Type (never a proof!): *)
formula EmptyHasNoElements =
  forall (z:Class). z in { x | Bot } -> Bot;

(* Uninhabited (false) formulas are legal Type definitions: *)
formula False_RussellIsSet = Set({ x | x in x -> Bot });
formula False_EveryClassIsSet = forall (X:Class). Set(X);
2. True Theorems (Inhabited by Kernel Proof Terms — Compile ✓)
theorem thm_empty_no_elements :
  forall (z:Class). z in { x | Bot } -> Bot =
  Lam (z:Class) => fn (hIn : z in { x | Bot }) =>
    snd((fst(compr(x. Bot, z)) hIn));

theorem thm_dunaev_proj :
  forall (A:Class). forall (B:Class).
    pr1([A, B]_D) = A /\ pr2([A, B]_D) = B =
  Lam (A:Class) => Lam (B:Class) => dunaev_proj(A, B);
3. False Statements (Deterministically Rejected by Kernel ✗)
(* REJECTED #1: Using a formula name as a proof term *)
theorem bad_1 : Set({ x | x in x -> Bot }) = False_RussellIsSet;
(* --> TypeError: Cannot use formula definition as a proof term *)

(* REJECTED #2: Packing proper class On into SetSort existential *)
theorem bad_on : exists (y:Set). y = On =
  pack(On, refl(On), exists (y:Set). y = On);
(* --> TypeError: Sort violation in EPack (Burali-Forti guard) *)

V, On, Model, ifdep, simple_if, isSet, [A, B]D, π1, π2, sss, NFV, FFI
8. Italic Red Class Variables (#f87171):
X, Y, Z, A, B, C, F, R (general classes); x, y, z, a, b, u, v (lowercase naming convention when a set is intended)

3.01 Axiom Class Comprehension Axiom
▸ Note
In Variant 1 (1st-Order NBG/MK), Class Comprehension is formalized at the metalevel as an axiom schema (class_comprehension_rul / class_comprehension_meta_axm_fm in foundations.ML, entry 4.06) parameterized by an arbitrary formula expression φ : Fm with side condition NFV(v_C, φ). In full Morse–Kelley (MK), φ may contain bound class variables (impredicative comprehension); in pure NBG, φ is predicative (quantifies only over sets) and is finitely axiomatizable via Bernays–Gödel class-existence axioms B1–B7. Lowercase x, y are used by naming convention because elements of classes must be sets (isSet(x)).

3.08 Axiom Subset-Sethood / Heredity Axiom (Subclasses of Sets are Sets)
▸ Note
Subset-Sethood (subclasses_of_sets_are_sets_entry, SML ID 3.12 in foundations.ML): any subclass A of a set b is itself a set (equivalent to the Separation Axiom). Note: this is distinct from Element-Sethood (x ∈ A → isSet(x)), which follows directly from the definition of sethood isSet(x) ⟷ ∃(Y : Class) (x ∈ Y) (SML ID 3.02, set_def_entry) and which Variant 2's Formulas-as-Types surface language exposes as the built-in primitive heredity(x, A) : x ∈ A → Set(x).

3.35 Definition Size Comparison Relation (A ⪯ B / lesseq)
▸ Note
Size comparison relation (lesseq_def_entry, 3.40 in foundations.ML): A ⪯ B holds iff there exists an injective class function f whose domain covers A (A ⊆ Dom(f)) and whose image on A is contained in B (f[A] ⊆ B). 3.68 Definition Semi-Singleton Subset Relation (s sss A)
▸ Note
Foundations ch. 110 (Semi-Singleton Subset, sss_def_entry, 3.36 in foundations.ML): binary infix relation (s sss A) asserting that s is a subclass of A with at most one element: (s ⊆ A) ∧ semi_singleton(s). For any class A (whether a set or a proper class), the sets s satisfying (s sss A) are ∅ and {a} for each element a ∈ A; hence their unary union reconstructs A itself: ⋃{ s | s sss A } = A (Theorem 110.1 in 110_family_evaluation.tex). By contrast, extracting the unique element a from a singleton class X = {a} uses unary intersection: Value(X) = ⋂{ y ∈ X | semi_singleton(X) } (Foundations 040_old_variant_of_iota_defs.tex §614 & 190_union_intersection.tex §65), so Value({a}) = ⋂{a} = a whereas Value(∅) = Value({a, b}) = ⋂∅ = V (proper class / nonset).

3.69 Theorem Theorem of Evaluation of a Family (F(x) = ⋃{ s | [x, s]_D ∈ F } and (Λx, t)(z) = t[z/x])
▸ Note
Foundations ch. 110 Theorem [evaluation of family] (family_eval_thm_entry, 3.37 in foundations.ML): for any family F, F(x) = ⋃{ s | [x, s]_D ∈ F }. For the lambda-encoded class family (Λ(x : Class), t) = { [x, s]_D | s sss t } ≡ { p | ∃(x : Class) ∃(s : Class) ((p = [x, s]_D) ∧ (s sss t)) } (which binds both x and s and stores all semi-singleton subsets s sss t), evaluating at any set argument z (under the capture-avoiding side condition FFI(z, v_x, (s sss t)) ∧ Fresh(v_s, v_x) ∧ NFV(v_s, t)) yields ((Λ(x : Class), t))(z) = ⋃{ s | s sss t[z/x] } = t[z/x] unconditionally—whether the fiber t[z/x] is a set (e.g. {1, 2}, where the semi-singleton subsets s are ∅, {1}, {2} and ⋃{∅, {1}, {2}} = {1, 2}) or a proper class.

▸ Note
Foundations ch. 130 (Classes as Types — Dependent Sum Σ, sigma_model_def_entry, 3.38 in foundations.ML): models the dependent pair type Σ_{x ∈ Dom(B)} B(x) as the class ΣB = { s | ∃(a : Class) ∃(b : Class) ((s = [a, b]_D) ∧ ((a ∈ Dom(B)) ∧ (b ∈ B(a)))) }. Because x ∈ Dom(B) and y ∈ B(x) are sets (by Heredity), their Dunaev pair [x, y]_D is also a set, so [x, y]_D ∈ ΣB holds iff x ∈ Dom(B) and y ∈ B(x).

3.71 Definition Set-Theoretic Model of Dependent Product (ΠB / Pi Predicate & Set-Section Models)
▸ Note
Foundations ch. 130 (Classes as Types — Dependent Product Π, lines 949–1086 of 130_classes_as_types.tex): provides two complementary models depending on whether the domain A = Dom(B) is a proper class or a set. (1) Model 1 — Conglomerate / Typing Predicate (f : ΠB) (general class domain Dom(B), pi_predicate_model_def_entry, 3.39 in foundations.ML): when Dom(B) is a proper class (such as V or On), a section f with Dom(f) = Dom(B) is itself a proper class and cannot be an element of a class comprehension { f | ... }; instead, (f : ΠB) is defined directly as the first-order predicate isFamily(f) ∧ (Dom(f) = Dom(B)) ∧ ∀(x ∈ Dom(B)) (f(x) ∈ B(x)). (2) Model 2 — Class of Set Sections ΠB (when isSet(Dom(B)) holds): when the domain A = Dom(B) is a set, every section f ⊆ ΣB with Dom(f) = A is a set (by Replacement and Union), so the class comprehension ΠB = { f ∈ 𝒫(ΣB) | isFunction(f) ∧ (Dom(f) = Dom(B)) ∧ ∀(x ∈ Dom(B)) (f(x) ∈ B(x)) } collects all dependent functions.

6.01 Axiom Theories (Metalevel Stratification)
▸ Note
Tarski hierarchy of theories with Henkin constants: W is an arbitrary theory, Q is Robinson arithmetic, T is recursive MK/NBG, and F is the Henkin-complete reflected extension. Because W, Q, T, F : Theory are metalevel theory expressions rather than classes, class inclusion ⊆ applies to their class models Model(W) ⊆ Model(Q) ⊆ Model(T) ⊆ Model(F) (where Model, implemented as CpEnc in typetheory.ML, maps an object-level typed term to its corresponding class term).

Unified Multi-Variant Architecture & Dual Semantics

Two Proof Assistant Variants, Decoupled Operators (Enc / Dec / Emb), and Option B Anatomy

Variant Bridge Verified (Poly/ML + CakeML)

Obelisk maintains two co-existing proof assistant variants in dedicated subdirectories of set_theory_prover/variants/, connected by an executable bidirectional translation bridge (program/variant_bridge.ML) and grounded in the dual semantics of program/types/typetheory.ML:

1. Variant 1 — Syntactical Proof Assistant (1st-Order, with ProofOf)
Open Dedicated Variant 1 Page →
Location: variants/variant1_first_order/ (newchecker.ML, types/typetheory.ML, types/foundations.ML)
Core Principle: Explicit syntactic datatypes (Fm, Ctx, Theory, Stmt, Prf) for 1st-order MK Class Theory statements about classes. Because statements (s : Stmt) are syntax trees (⟨...⟩ / ⟦...⟧) rather than ambient types, connecting a proof term to the statement it proves requires ProofOf / ProofsOf: (p : ProofOf(s)) (and via Gödel encoding Enc, (Enc(p) ∈ ProofsOf(Enc(s))) and (Enc(s) ∈ Theorems)).
2. Variant 2 — Semantical Proof Assistant (Rocq / Higher-Order)
Open Dedicated Variant 2 Page →
Location: variants/variant2_higher_order/ (nbg_compiler.ML, nbg_surface_compiler.ML, dependent_eval.ML)
Core Principle: Rocq / Curry–Howard dependent type theory where propositions/formulas are types directly (Theorem name : φ, prf : φ): implications are function spaces, quantifiers are dependent products/sums, and proofs are constructive λ-terms—no ProofOf wrapper or quotation brackets ⟨...⟩ needed.
Decoupled Brackets (⟨...⟩ / ⟦...⟧) vs. Special Functional Symbols (Enc, Dec, Emb)
  • Quotation ⟨...⟩ (‹...›) & Antiquotation / Valuation ⟦...⟧ ([|...|]): Purely syntax-splicing and valuation brackets from program/libs/unicodedefs.ML. Inside ⟨...⟩, antiquoting a class variable ⟦X⟧ splices the class X itself—which may be a proper class like V or On! Therefore, isSet(⟦X⟧) is NOT automatically true (e.g. ¬isSet(V) by Russell's theorem).
  • Syntactic Encoding Enc(s) (CpEnc in typetheory.ML): Maps any syntactic object (s : T) (Fm, Stmt, Prf, Ctx, Theory) to its finite Gödel/hereditarily-finite set code in (V_ω ⊂ V). Because every finite syntax tree code is a finite set, isSet(Enc(s)) IS unconditionally true!
  • Syntactic Decoding Dec(c, T) (VDec in typetheory.ML): Partially decodes a set code (c : Class) back into target syntactic collection (T : Col), satisfying the roundtrip law ∀(s : T) (Dec(Enc(s), T) = s).
  • Dual Type Embedding Emb(T) (LTpEmb / TyTpEmb in typetheory.ML): Captures the Dual Semantics of typetheory.ML: (A) Semantic Predicate Interpretation: (Emb(Class)(X) ⟷ ⊤) (so Emb(Class)(V) is a theorem!) and (Emb(Set)(X) ⟷ isSet(X)) (so ¬Emb(Set)(V) is Russell's theorem); (B) Syntactic Code-Class Interpretation: for syntactic types (T ∈ {Fm, Stmt, Prf, Ctx, Theory}), (Emb(T)(x) ⟷ (x ∈ CodeClass(T))), where (CodeClass(T) = { c | (isSet(c) ∧ ∃(s : T) (c = Enc(s))) }).

Machine-Checked Standard Library (Both Variants)

NBG Formulas-as-Types & 1st-Order Bridged Theorems

30 kernel-checked theorems

Each row is a closed proof term in examples/nbg_verified_programs.nbg, compiled by NBGSurfaceCompiler (Variant 2 — Semantical / Formulas-as-Types, where a formula φ is a type directly: Theorem name : φ) and automatically translated by VariantBridge into a 7-part Option B 1st-order NBG certificate (Variant 1 — Syntactical / 1st-Order, where (thm : Stmt) is a syntax tree and verification uses ProofsOf and Theorems) in Poly/ML and CakeML.

The 69-entry axiomatic & metatheoretic catalog is audited separately: 18 derived theorems, 36 conservative definitions (including Enc, Dec, Emb, ProofsOf, Theorems), 8 primitive inference rules, and 7 irreducible MK/NBG axioms (alongside the 46 raw kernel entries exported from foundations.ML in sml_kernel_export.json). Definitional and axiomatic witnesses are never counted as derived theorems, and the kernel rejects the untrusted PCheat_prf placeholder on every certified path.

Reading Guide — Decoding cantor_diagonal_theorem (Dunaev Tagged Pairs & Diagonal Class): In class theory without primitive function application, an indexed family of classes \( \{ F(x) \}_{x \in S} \) is represented by a single class relation \( F \) of Dunaev tagged ordered pairs \( [x, z]_D \) such that \( ([x, z]_D \in F) \longleftrightarrow (z \in F(x)) \). Define Cantor's anti-diagonal class \( D = \{ x \mid ((x \in S) \land (([x, x]_D \in F) \to \bot)) \} \). Then for any index \( x \in S \), if the \( x \)-th fiber \( F(x) \) coincided with \( D \) (i.e. \( \forall z\; ((z \in D) \longleftrightarrow ([x, z]_D \in F)) \)), instantiating \( z := x \) yields the diagonal equivalence \( ((x \in D) \longleftrightarrow ([x, x]_D \in F)) \), which together with \( ((x \in D) \longleftrightarrow ((x \in S) \land \neg([x, x]_D \in F))) \) derives \( \bot \). Thus no class family indexed by \( S \) can surject onto all subclasses of \( S \).
